h1:
🏅 Best Michelin restaurants in Nonthaburi
Two stars next door to Bangkok
intro: Nonthaburi sits right across the river from Bangkok, yet it hides two one-star kitchens: Akkee, where Thai cooking meets live fire and a hard-to-get reservation, and Suan Thip, a riverside teak house that eats more relaxed. Round it out with five Bib Gourmands, from the seafood at Chai to the fiery jungle curry at Kaeng Pa Loong Sa-Nga.
quickAnswerHtml: Nonthaburi has 7 Michelin 2026 restaurants: 2 one-stars (Akkee, Suan Thip) and 5 Bib Gourmands.

blocks.html: Nonthaburi sits right across the river from Bangkok, yet it hides two one-star kitchens: Akkee, where Thai cooking meets live fire and a hard-to-get reservation, and Suan Thip, a riverside teak house that eats more relaxed. Round it out with five Bib Gourmands, from the seafood at Chai to the fiery jungle curry at Kaeng Pa Loong Sa-Nga.

blocks.name: Akkee
blocks.descHtml:
The main cost is the dinner set menu at THB 3,850 per person (add-ons not included), plus the Thai craft beer and sato pairing — seven glasses for another THB 1,550 — if you want to go all out, or you can order a la carte instead. Booking goes through the widget at akkeerestaurant.com/reservation (eRestaurants system), by phone at (+66) 82 561 4691, or via LINE — seating is a small counter, so always book ahead, especially for Saturday-Sunday lunch, which fills up faster than anything else. Important note: the tasting menu has no seafood-free or vegan version.

The restaurant is in Pak Kret, Nonthaburi. Hours are dinner 17:30-23:00 on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday, with Saturday-Sunday adding lunch from 12:00-15:00. Closed every Wednesday. The most reliable way there is by car or taxi/Grab — the Pink Line's Pak Kret Bypass station (PK07) is the closest station, but the walking distance from the station to the restaurant hasn't been confirmed, so grabbing a Grab from the station is the safest plan. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: "Lost recipe" Thai dishes revived from old cookbooks, cooked over charcoal with all-Thai ingredients
mustOrder: The lost-recipe set menu revived from ancient Thai cookbooks
The eastern-seaboard set — Gulf of Thailand seafood with wild foraged herbs
The Thai craft beer and sato pairing — seven glasses
blocks.bestFor: Fans of ancient Thai cooking who want to taste lost recipes revived from old cookbooks, and anyone who loves an intimate tasting counter beside a charcoal kitchen

blocks.name: Suan Thip
blocks.descHtml:
Suan Thip sits on the Chao Phraya riverside in Pak Kret, Nonthaburi, with no train station within walking distance. The most convenient way there is by car or ride-hail via Soi Sukhaprachasan 2 Soi 9 or Soi Wat Ku. The restaurant is open daily 11:00–21:30, with a la carte mains running about 500–1,000 THB per person, while the Suan Thip-style khao chae set is 435 THB, sold only during April and selling out fast.

Booking is by phone directly with the restaurant only, at 02-583-3748, 02-583-4540, or 082-366-9696 — MICHELIN notes the restaurant takes its own bookings with no online platform. Weekends get busy with large family groups, so if you want the riverside pavilion, the best seating in the house, call several days ahead and state your preference directly. The best time to go is a weekday lunch, with good light and lighter crowds, and if you're set on the khao chae, call ahead before you head out to check it's still available that day. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Lotus-petal miang kham and the Suan Thip-style khao chae, sold only in April
mustOrder: Khi lek curry with grilled fish/catfish
blocks.bestFor: Family meals/bringing the elders for royal Thai cooking on the riverside, and fans of old-style Thai food who want to try authentic khao chae in April

blocks.name: Chai
blocks.descHtml:
Budget per head around THB 250–500 is light for a Bib Gourmand-level restaurant — crab fried rice starts at THB 75, squid in fish sauce THB 230, fried grouper with fish sauce THB 390, and the large curry-powder sea crab THB 800. The restaurant takes cash only, so bring enough. Most tables are walk-in, but if you're coming as a larger group you can call ahead at 063-998-3986 or 088-978-1558 — no deposit needed, and no online queue system to fight over.

The restaurant is open 15:00–01:00 (Sundays until around midnight) and closed on the second and fourth Tuesday of every month. Early evening is busiest, so if you'd rather skip the wait, go in the late afternoon or after 9pm. Getting there means driving or taking a taxi to Soi Samakkhi 38, Tha Sai, Mueang Nonthaburi, since the MRT Pink Line's Samakkhi station is over 2 km away — too far to walk. On the plus side, the restaurant has its own car park and an air-con zone to sit in. Read the full review →
blocks.area: Soi Samakkhi 38, Tha Sai, Mueang Nonthaburi
blocks.signature: Fried grouper with fish sauce — crisp skin, tender flesh, whole fish for THB 390
blocks.bestFor: A late-night meal with friends or family who want serious seafood at khao tom prices — best for people with a car, since the location isn't within walking distance of any train station
blocks.zone: Soi Samakkhi 38, Tha Sai, Mueang Nonthaburi
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Chai Phochana official Facebook page

blocks.name: Chang-Wang-Imm
blocks.descHtml:
Budget runs around 500–1,000 baht per head, with most vegetable and curry dishes priced 160–290 baht. What pushes the budget up are two pricier items: the grilled giant river prawn at around 850 baht each, and the fried sea bass miang at 450–600 baht. Booking matters a lot, especially if you want the riverside pavilion with a view of Koh Kret's leaning chedi — that section always fills up first. Call 085-525-9242 or 064-060-4390, or message the restaurant's Facebook page ahead of time. No deposit is required based on available information, but you should still book rather than queue up at the door.

There's no rail access, so you'll need to drive or grab a taxi to Soi Wat Bang Chak, Chaiyaphruek Road, Bang Tanai, Pak Kret. The restaurant has parking. Open daily from 11:00, though closing time varies by source (Wongnai lists 20:00, while older reviews say 22:00–23:00) — call ahead to confirm before an evening meal to be safe. The best time to go is after 18:30, when the outdoor seating starts to cool down, and Friday–Saturday nights bring live music. Read the full review →
blocks.area: Chao Phraya riverside, Bang Tanai, Pak Kret (opposite Koh Kret)
blocks.signature: Grilled giant river prawn and old-recipe kaeng kua bai ra with prawns, eaten riverside across from Koh Kret's leaning chedi
mustOrder: Kaeng kua bai ra with prawns
blocks.bestFor: Family riverside meals, views of Koh Kret's leaning chedi, and anyone hunting for old-recipe Thai curries at Bib Gourmand prices
blocks.zone: Chao Phraya riverside, Bang Tanai, Pak Kret (opposite Koh Kret)
blocks.hours: Daily from 11:00; closing time varies by source (Wongnai say

blocks.name: Hong Seng
blocks.descHtml:
Budget per person runs about THB 251–500 and up — most vegetable dishes and fried items are in the low hundreds, but the grilled giant river prawns are priced by size, so the bigger the prawn, the higher the bill, and the restaurant is cash only — worth remembering, so withdraw cash before you go. Booking is by calling the restaurant directly at 02-583-8631 or 02-583-7654 — they manage their own queue entirely, with no online booking system available.

The time to plan around carefully is weekdays, since the restaurant only serves lunch, opening around 10:00–10:30 (sources differ) and closing at 2pm sharp. On Saturdays, Sundays, and public holidays it stays open until 4pm. The riverside wooden terrace tables are always the first to go on weekends, so arrive before noon if you want the Chao Phraya view. There are three ways to get there — take the Pink Line to Pak Kret Junction station (PK06) and walk about 20 minutes or grab a 5-minute motorbike taxi; drive and park in the public space under the Rama IV Bridge; or take a boat straight to the Pak Kret pier next to the restaurant, exactly as MICHELIN itself recommends. Read the full review →
blocks.area: Pak Kret riverside (foot of Rama IV Bridge, next to Pak Kret municipal pier), Nonthaburi
blocks.signature: Grilled giant river prawns with spicy seafood dipping sauce
mustOrder: Grilled giant river prawns with spicy seafood dipping sauce
Mini deep-fried crab meat rolls wrapped in tofu skin
Stir-fried bitter gourd with salted fish
Kale stems stir-fried with prawn claws
Mango sticky rice with coconut milk
blocks.bestFor: A riverside lunch with the family — grilled giant river prawns on the wooden terrace of a 60-plus-year-old Pak Kret institution
blocks.zone: Pak Kret riverside (foot of Rama IV Bridge, next to Pak Kret municipal pier), Nonthaburi

blocks.name: Kaeng Pa Loong Sa-Nga
blocks.descHtml:
Budget per person runs around THB 101–250, with most standout dishes in the THB 120–230 range — kaeng pa with grey-featherback fish balls at THB 120–170, kaeng pa with venison at THB 200, tom yum river catfish at THB 230, while the fried horse mackerel with fish sauce is the priciest at around THB 390. It's a walk-in restaurant with no online booking system; if you're coming as a large group, you can call ahead on 02-952-9992. Open daily 10:00–21:00 (some listings say until 22:00), but remember it's closed on the 16th of every month without fail.

Getting there is the main challenge with this restaurant. It sits in Soi Ngamwongwan 23 (Soi Wat Buakwan), about 500 meters in from the mouth of the soi, with no rail line reaching the door. The nearest stations are MRT Khae Rai (Pink Line) and Nonthaburi Civic Center (Purple Line), both about 3 kilometers away. Taking a taxi or motorbike taxi from either station is the most convenient option. Driving yourself is easier still, since the restaurant has its own car park. Go for lunch or an early dinner before dark for the fullest menu and the most comfortable seating. Read the full review →
blocks.area: Soi Ngamwongwan 23 / Wat Buakwan area, Bang Kraso–Bang Khen, Mueang Nonthaburi
blocks.cuisine: Central Thai food / Bold jungle curry
blocks.signature: Kaeng pa with grey-featherback fish balls
mustOrder: Kaeng pa with grey-featherback fish balls
Fried horse mackerel with fish sauce
blocks.bestFor: A family or friend-group meal for people who can handle real heat, craving home-style central Thai jungle curry at MICHELIN level for just over a hundred baht
blocks.foodType: Central Thai food / Bold jungle curry
blocks.hours: Daily 10:00–21:00 (some listings say 22:00); closed on the 1

blocks.name: SANN
blocks.descHtml:
Budget per person runs around 500–1,000 THB à la carte — small dishes like som chun start at THB 120, up to crab curry with chakhram leaves at THB 540, an easy price for a brand-new Bib Gourmand restaurant. There's no booking platform of any kind — you'll need to call 066-137-6749 or message the restaurant's official Facebook/Instagram page directly. Because it just earned its Bib Gourmand in 2026, weekends will noticeably get busier, so calling ahead every time is recommended, especially for a weekend lunch.

Getting there means driving — the restaurant is on Bang Yai–Bang Khu Lat Road, Bang Yai district, Nonthaburi, and the nearest Purple Line MRT stations near Bang Yai are more than 3 km away, so walking isn't practical. The restaurant has its own car park and accepts credit cards. Hours per MICHELIN are daily 11:00–22:00 (Wongnai lists Mon–Thu 11:00–21:00, Fri–Sun 11:00–22:00). If you want a seat in the open-air garden-view section without the heat, a weekday lunch or an evening after the sun has eased off is the best time to go. Read the full review →
blocks.area: Bang Yai–Bang Khu Lat Road, Bang Len, Bang Yai, Nonthaburi (Ratchaphruek orchard belt)
blocks.signature: Palm-shoot curry with grilled pork — young palm shoots in fresh-pressed coconut milk with grilled pork, the dish MICHELIN's inspectors singled out directly
mustOrder: Flash-fried river prawn dusted with sea salt
blocks.bestFor: A weekend family meal · for fans of rare provincial Thai recipes · for anyone with a car who wants to drive out of town to eat
blocks.zone: Bang Yai–Bang Khu Lat Road, Bang Len, Bang Yai, Nonthaburi (Ratchaphruek orchard belt)

faq.q: Which restaurant should I book first?
faq.a: Akkee, the one-star doing Thai cooking over live fire, has few seats and a long wait, so reserve several days ahead. Suan Thip seats more people in its riverside house, but weekends still fill up, so call ahead.

faq.q: What is the more affordable way to try a Michelin star here?
faq.a: Suan Thip is the value pick among the stars, around 500 to 1,000 baht a head for a shared Thai spread by the water. Akkee is a pricier tasting experience, better saved for a special night out.

faq.q: What are the Bib Gourmand spots in Nonthaburi?
faq.a: There are five: Chai for seafood, Hong Seng for Thai-Chinese cooking, the punchy Kaeng Pa Loong Sa-Nga, plus Chang-Wang-Imm and Sann, both Thai. All are easier on the wallet than the starred kitchens.

faq.q: Is it easy to reach Nonthaburi from Bangkok?
faq.a: Very. Nonthaburi borders Bangkok, so the MRT Purple Line or a short drive across the bridge gets you there. Several spots like Suan Thip and Chai sit by the river, so go early to beat the traffic.

faq.q: Where should I go if I love bold, spicy food?
faq.a: Head to Kaeng Pa Loong Sa-Nga for its herb-heavy jungle curry, roughly 120 to 170 baht a plate. For fresh seafood instead, Chai is the pick.
